key_insight: Epitaxial kagome CoSn exhibits efficient spin-charge conversion, with an effective spin Hall angle about 11 times that of the measured Pt reference.
engineering_relevance: CoSn is a promising spin-orbit torque material for low-power spintronic devices.
method: Atomic-resolution scanning tunneling microscopy and dI/dV spectroscopy probe CoSn surfaces and flat-band signatures.
Magneto-optical measurements quantify spin-orbit torque in Ni/CoSn bilayers.
DFT calculations investigate intrinsic spin Hall effects and momentum-space Berry curvature.
evidence_signal: The reported effective spin Hall angle is 0.484 ± 0.005 for CoSn versus 0.0436 ± 0.0003 for Pt in Ni-based bilayers.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish device-level power savings or how performance depends on film quality and interface properties.
paper_title: Spin-Charge Conversion in an Epitaxial Kagome Flat-Band Metal
